content.thinking:
Scratch/phoenix exists, so I'll confirm the builder method signatures and path types before writing the actual implementation, importing THREE and the builder creation helper.

Writing the feather geometry function...

Checking that the tip width stays reasonable at around 1mm, and confirming the membrane options like cols and thickness are valid. Feather paint is cheap to create per feather since caching isn't really necessary, and the texel evaluation cost for baking should be manageable even at high resolution.

Now I'm defining the color palette (deep reds, crimsons, oranges, ambers, golds) and writing the feather paint function that blends tones based on chevron and zigzag patterns to create the barb and rachis coloring...

Picking a flame-like color palette, moving from deep red through crimson, scarlet, orange into amber and yellow, with slightly different band sequences for primaries, secondaries, and coverts to vary the feather groups.

Working out the body paint layers, with a scaled coat pattern for the back blending scarlet into deep red, and a separate chest coat shifting through amber and gold tones, then combining them with a fur-edge effect so each region keeps its own lit/dark shading.

I'm checking the furEdge axis orientation against surface normals at different body points — top of back, rump, sides, belly — to verify where the boundary between back and chest coloring falls based on the level and axis values.

Now for the head, I'm planning a similar boundary function for the crown vs. face mask, using a horizontal plane near the head's vertical center with a small transition zone, and considering where to set the level so the eyes end up placed within the cream-colored facial area.

For colors, I'm leaning toward a cream-gold face ("#ffe9a8") with crimson scales on the crown, and choosing fiery iris tones like "#ff5a1c" with a lighter highlight "#ffd27a" so the eyes read clearly against the pale face, plus a soft blush tone to warm the cheeks.

I'm keeping the expressive brow stroke since it reads well near the crest, and designing gold scale patterns for the legs with a darker edge tone and a crimson feather puff at the thigh. For the toes I'm deciding between cream-toned talons or a dark plum accent to finish the gold scale pattern.

For the chest ruff, I'm building a feather card SVG that clips a layered shape so the root sits at the bottom of the drawing and the tip points upward, then stacking colored bands moving from the root toward the tip. Writing feather clip-path code...

Designing the remaining feather textures plus flame wisp and tassel SVGs, keeping atlas costs small and defining glow colors and curve shapes for each element.

Since the tassel hangs upside down relative to the card orientation, I'm drawing it inverted: gold cap and bead at the SVG's bottom, with cord strands fanning upward toward the top edge so it reads correctly once mounted.

Now sketching the filigree medallion decal for the chest, aiming for a symmetrical design...

Still writing filigree SVG paths...

For the chest gem, I'm shaping a glowing ruby teardrop using an octahedron scaled taller, with a bright white-yellow core, and planning a matching gem for the forehead circlet, plus scattering neck ruff details across the body's sweep geometry.

Now I'm setting up two scatter passes for card-shaped feather elements along the neck and chest, filtering hits by height and normal direction, orienting them to flow down and back along the body, and assigning gold-plume texture to chest/belly hits versus crimson for the rest.

I'm also planning extra feather rings on the thighs, ankles, and wing roots, plus a crimson tube for the tail base chain. Sizing out the card lengths and counts per region, and estimating triangle budget based on bend-curl segments—landing around 5-6k triangles total, which should keep things light.

Now I'm working out wing trail flame cards—orienting them to stand upright at feather tips, deciding whether to use a cross-facing setup so they're visible from both front/back and above/below views.

Next I'm sketching the rig structure, laying out joint positions for the pelvis, belly, chest, and neck chain as a series of 3D points that will form the spine's curve.

Still defining joint chains...

Sweeping the tail tube with a crimson gradient narrowing from .09 to .05, then laying out the leg chains symmetrically for left and right sides—hip, knee, ankle, and foot joints with ground contact points defined for each foot.

Working out the leg segment lengths (thigh, shin, tarsus) and tapering their sweep radii along each chain, with the thighs puffed out as feathered "pants" in crimson and the tarsus scaled down in gold to mimic bird-leg scaling. Setting up color bands per chain so the coat transitions into the gold scale texture partway down.

Now I'm positioning the toes relative to the foot ball joint, defining three front toes splayed at angles with tapering radii down to small tips, plus a curved talon spike at each tip angled forward and down for a claw-like finish.

Then I'm figuring out toe joint naming conventions and parenting them to the chain tip of each leg, adding a fourth hind-facing toe, and starting to work out the wing's shoulder joint attachment point off the chest vertebra.

Working out wing geometry and feather placement...

Setting up joint attachments for each feather group, then defining tertials and primaries with their own root positions, angles, lengths, and widths, each attached to the appropriate skeletal parent.

Working out the outer wing extent so the fan spreads correctly, then setting up the up/cross vectors for feather curvature. I'm layering the coverts now—greater coverts hugging the secondary bases, median coverts slightly forward and smaller, each with its own length and width tweaks for a natural stacked look.

Now I'm pinning primary coverts to match the primaries, picking a golden amber-to-cream palette for coverts to contrast the dark crimson flight feathers for a nice brightness gradient across the wing. I'm tallying joint counts per wing to make sure the covert rows map to the right bones (elbow, wrist, shoulder), then moving on to the tail fan—nine short feathers spreading symmetrically from the tail's end joint, angled backward.

Still working out tail feather geometry and streamers...

Adding slight lateral curve for visual variation, and double-checking the floor clearance near the ribbon's lowest point before finalizing the tail's extension.

The body spans roughly 3.8 meters front to back with a 5 meter wingspan, so the camera framing should handle it fine. I'm tweaking the tail length slightly and setting up the streamer sweep with an elliptical cross-section to get a flat, flame-like ribbon look rather than a rounded one.

Switching to a box section instead so each flat face catches light distinctly, giving a cel-shaded appearance. Now I'm working out the width taper function for the ribbon — narrow near the base, widening partway, then tapering to a sharp point at the tip, with an eye-spot marker placed around the midpoint.

For the streamer's head crest, I'm positioning plumes relative to the head joint using local offsets — placing a center plume and side plumes that curl upward and backward from their base points.

Setting `up: [1,0,0]` orients the crest ribbons as vertical flame sheets rather than flat horizontal ones, which works for the side plumes too. Now I'm thinking through ear plumes as long streamers sweeping back and down from the sides of the head, flowing elegantly toward the back.

I'm planning gold-to-orange ribbon tassels hanging per side, plus scattering glowing flame cards along wing tips and trailing edges — roughly 40 small cards built from cross-plane triangles for the embers effect. For the beak, I'm settling on a flat amber gold with a cream highlight tone, since flat color strings are fine for small details like this.

Now I'm deciding on material strategy: I'll use cel-shading for the prominent colored parts like the beak and gold ornaments, since even tiny studs and spheres look good with that toon-style half-lit/half-dark shading, while glowing elements and gems stay as flat emissive colors instead. I'm also sketching out the wing ornamentation — gold wrist bracers with rings and tassels, a leading-edge band at the shoulder, and filigree decals on the wing surface.

I realize the chest decal placement could conflict with scattered cards covering that area, so I need to add a keep-out filter excluding points too close to the gem center before scattering.

Writing SVG flame wisp...

Now I'm sketching out a feather SVG with a zigzag pattern, then planning a symmetrical filigree ornament around 120×100 centered at (60,52), with a gold ring for the gem socket and radiating petal shapes around it.

Writing SVG filigree code...

Then I'm planning the chest decal placement on the body mesh, sizing it to fit the surface sweep so the gold artwork renders directly on the textured part rather than flat shading.

For the gem, I'm figuring out where to place it using a raycast against the chest surface to get an accurate position and normal, then building an octahedron gem stuck into that point with some embed depth, followed by a gold lathed bezel ring whose profile and orientation align with the surface normal at that hit point.

I'm considering whether to add extra gold details like studs or a gorget around the body, but deciding to focus on the face instead — cheeks, beak, nostril, eye decals, crimson brow ridges, and a gold circlet with a gem, while skipping side ornaments. Now I'm planning to write the full file, keeping in mind that surface hits need to come from the skull part's sphere geometry and its paint setup.

Now I'm working out the head's paint logic, positioning the head center relative to the neck joint, and setting up crest tufts as a chain parented to the head using Catmull-Rom points with an "up" direction to control roll. I'm figuring out the sweep radius function for the crest, reasoning through how the tangent, normal, and binormal vectors interact with the chosen up vector to determine the vertical versus sideways thickness of the shape.

I'm also planning the plume color gradient with amber-to-cream banding, the wing arm tube skinning with crimson scale coloring, thigh feather cards scattered along the leg, and now working through toe chain generation—building Catmull-Rom point paths for each digit, picking the correct parent joint from the leg's tip or last joint, and naming the toe segments for multi-span chains.

Toe sweeping with hexagonal cross-sections for flatter undersides, spiked talons oriented along a forward-down vector bound to the last toe joint, and small gold knuckle spheres placed at each toe midpoint. Now I'm setting up anklet rings by sweeping a closed loop path around the tarsus at a point along the leg chain.

I'm figuring out tassel placement off the anklet loop, sampling points along the loop path for frame orientation and testing which angle corresponds to the front of the leg, while keeping the body cards' default flow pointing back and down. I'll skip adding a ring element elsewhere, reserving that approach for hair instead.

Now I'm structuring the wing-building function to handle both left and right sides symmetrically, computing feather directions from side-dependent outward vectors combined with angle-based sine/cosine blending, plus cross products to get feather widths that stay consistent when the sign flips. Each feather gets its own joint aimed along its direction vector, and I'm setting up per-feather paint closures so eyespots and color sweeps can vary across the feather group while sharing a texture atlas.

Writing wing geometry code...

Still defining chains...

Then I add a jaw joint attached to head, positioned forward and down slightly with an aim point further forward, using head-relative coordinates. Now I'm setting up the body sweep, binding it to the spine and neck bones with color...

I'm bumping body sides to 12 to avoid the octagon-faceted look from the default 8-sided circles. Now I'm defining the tail chain as a bone hierarchy branching from the hips, using a short catmull-rom path of three points curving down and back to form the tail base, midpoint, and tip, then building the tail tube geometry around it.

Checking that leg and body proportions sit sensibly: body radius and belly height look fine relative to hip placement, and I'm sketching the leg joint chain (hip, knee, ankle, foot) with segment lengths for the tibia and tarsus coming out reasonable. Now I'm defining the thigh puff sweep radii that taper down toward the knee and shin.

The band split at t=.52 creates an abrupt tube junction where pants meet scaly leg, visible mainly as a colour transition since radius changes only slightly there; I'll let the feathery cards hanging from the pants cover that seam.

Now I'm thinking through the leg contact point, wing arm radii and shoulder puff sphere, body paint shader for the wing arm using scales, glow hit positions at feather tips, and how flame-textured cards at primary tip frames will need to find the nearest joint bone since literal-position frames have none attached.

Instead I realize I can use the joint's own moved frame, which preserves the bone and orientation while shifting to the tip position — that way each flame card extends naturally along the feather's direction past its tip, and I can collect all these frames into a single cards call across every feather with flame texture, cross-facing, and a defined size.

I'm sizing the flame cards small with some randomized variation and a decent glow strength, and planning similar flame treatment for the head crest tips and streamer ends using the same tip-joint frame trick. I'm skipping loose floating embers since disconnected parts would violate the "nothing hangs above it" constraint, but I need to double check how `joint.moved(p)` actually interprets the point argument — whether it's in the frame's local axes or world coordinates — since getting that wrong would misplace all the flame cards.
